title: U.S. House · Oregon's 4th District
area: Southwestern Oregon, including Eugene/Springfield, the central coast, and the counties along the California border west of the Cascades.

context.text: Incumbent Val Hoyle defeated Melissa Bird and Dan Bahlen with 75.1% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Monique DeSpain defeated Stefan Strek 86.6%-12.4% in the Republican primary. DeSpain also won the Libertarian ballot line and Justin Filip is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee.

summary.text: Val Hoyle is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election to Oregon's 4th Congressional District, which she has represented since January 2023. Before Congress she spent 25 years in the international bicycle industry, then served in the Oregon House of Representatives, including as Majority Leader, and as Oregon's Labor Commissioner. In the U.S. House she sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Natural Resources committees.

background.text: Born on Travis Air Force Base in Fairfield, California; according to her office, her father was a firefighter and labor leader and her mother organized in support of the 1972 Equal Rights Amendment. Ballotpedia lists her birth year as 1964.

First in her family to earn a college degree: began at Bunker Hill Community College and graduated from Emmanuel College with a bachelor's degree in political science and a concentration in international studies (Ballotpedia lists the degree year as 1992).

Spent 25 years working in the international bicycle industry in retail management, manufacturing distribution and international trade; Ballotpedia also lists work as a director at United Way of Lane County and as a policy fellow at the Wayne Morse Center for Law and Politics.
Served in the Oregon House of Representatives for West Eugene and Junction City (District 14) until 2017, including as House Majority Leader (2013 to 2015 per Ballotpedia).
Ran in the 2016 Democratic primary for Oregon Secretary of State, finishing second to Brad Avakian.
Won the nonpartisan Oregon Commissioner of Labor and Industries primary outright in May 2018 and served as Labor Commissioner, leading the Bureau of Labor and Industries, from 2019 to 2023.

Won the open 4th District seat in November 2022 (succeeding Peter DeFazio) and was sworn into the 118th Congress in January 2023; re-elected in 2024 over Republican Monique DeSpain and Pacific Green Justin Filip.

Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the House Committee on Natural Resources, and belongs to caucuses including the Congressional Progressive Caucus, New Democrat Coalition and Labor Caucus.
According to her office, she and her husband Stephen are both union members and moved to Lane County over 25 years ago to raise their two children.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittees on Indian and Insular Affairs; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Subcommittees on Highways and Transit; Water Resources and Environment).

summary.text: Monique DeSpain is the Republican and Libertarian nominee for Oregon's 4th Congressional District. She is a retired Air Force colonel who spent 20 years as a Judge Advocate General's Corps lawyer, then worked as an attorney and policy advocate in Oregon. She was the Republican nominee against Rep. Val Hoyle in 2024 and, according to her Ballotpedia survey, describes herself as an outsider running on public safety, border security and cost-of-living issues.

background.text: Born in Long Beach, California; says she made Oregon her home in 1995 when she left active duty to attend law school at Willamette University in Salem.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Utah (1986), a graduate degree from Central Michigan University (1993), and a law degree from Willamette University College of Law (1998).

Served 30 years in the U.S. Air Force, Air Force Reserve and Oregon Air National Guard, retiring as a colonel; 20 of those years were as a Judge Advocate General's (JAG) Corps lawyer, with postings including Singapore, Bosnia, Kosovo, Cyprus, Italy, the Pentagon and Oregon, handling investigations, litigation and military justice advice.

Alongside her military service, practiced law on business and family matters, veterans' affairs and dispute resolution, and volunteered for ten years as a board member and mediator with the Center for Dialogue and Resolution in Eugene.

After retiring from the military in 2019, joined the Kevin Mannix Law Firm, working on cases for crime victims and business owners; in 2022 she joined the nonprofit Common Sense for Oregon, working on policy on homelessness, addiction and crime.
Was the Republican nominee for the 4th District in 2024, losing the general election to Val Hoyle, 43.9% to 51.7%.
Won the Republican primary on May 19, 2026, to become the party's nominee again; she also appears on the Libertarian line.
Describes herself as a single mother who raised twin sons in Eugene.

priorities.text: Public safety and homelessness: says the district has seen 'rampant homelessness, unsafe streets, rising costs' and calls for law-enforcement collaboration and addiction/mental-illness-focused solutions to homelessness.
Border security: says she supports 'constant vigilance to stop the flow of human trafficking, fentanyl, and other deadly drugs' into the country.
Government spending: says she would end what she calls 'reckless tax-and-spend policies fueling inflation.'

positions.summary: Says she will ensure the nation's borders remain secure and supports continued vigilance against human trafficking and drug trafficking across them.
positions.quote: I will ensure our nation's borders remain secure. I support constant vigilance to stop the flow of human trafficking, fentanyl, and other deadly drugs into our nation.

positions.summary: Supports collaboration between law enforcement at all levels to reduce crime and keep communities safe.

candidates.name: Justin Filip

summary.text: Justin Filip is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee for Oregon's 4th Congressional District. A University of Oregon graduate who worked as a program coordinator at the university, he has held party leadership roles in the Pacific Green Party since 2021. This is his second run for the seat; according to his campaign, his priorities include reducing military spending, addressing homelessness and protecting federal lands.

background.text: Born in Michigan and moved to Oregon in 1995; earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from the University of Oregon.
Described himself in 2024 as a Program Coordinator at the University of Oregon, and in April 2024 co-founded the UO Faculty and Staff for Justice in Palestine, according to his campaign site.
Served on the Pacific Green Party's State Coordinating Committee from 2021 to 2024 and is the party's secretary and co-chair of its Eugene chapter.
First ran for office in 2024 as the Pacific Green candidate in the 4th District, receiving 10,315 votes (2.7%) against Val Hoyle's 195,862.

Other roles listed on Ballotpedia include cultural development chair of the Buena Vista Parent Organization and a seat on the Eugene Figure Skating Club board; has volunteered with the Egan Warming Centers and as a youth baseball coach.

priorities.text: His 2024 campaign website stated his top priorities as ending U.S. military involvement in the conflict in Gaza and reducing military spending, bringing federal dollars to the district to address housing and homelessness, protecting federal lands, and advancing high-speed rail in the Pacific Northwest.

candidates.researchNotes: Filip has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; priorities are drawn from his 2024 campaign website as archived by Ballotpedia, and no updated 2026 statements were found.
